description: A `--self-host` run mode for the `scp-node` reference binary that selects the already-specced `no_domain()` deployment path (NAT-PMP/UPnP port mapping + STUN + did:dht publish + broadcast site projection) so an operator can host a static website behind a cone NAT with no manual port-forward and no domain. The mechanism is fully specified (§10.12 reachability tiers, §10.12.8 ApplicationNode Integration, §18.6 ApplicationNode, §18.11.12 SiteConfig) and implemented (ApplicationNodeBuilder::no_domain, enable_broadcast_projection_with_site, commit_deploy). This PRD wires that mechanism into the shipped binary as an opt-in run mode and proves it end to end.

stories.title: Add --self-host flag and SCP_NODE_SELF_HOST env selection (opt-in, non-default upnp feature)
stories.description: The shipped `scp-node` binary mandates `SCP_NODE_DOMAIN` and always takes the `.domain()` path (`crates/scp-node/src/main.rs`), so the binary itself never calls `no_domain()` and does no NAT traversal. This story adds an opt-in self-host run mode: a `--self-host` CLI flag and a `SCP_NODE_SELF_HOST` environment variable that select the `.no_domain()` deployment path described in §10.12.8 ('Behavior when `.no_domain()` is set'). Self-host mode MUST be opt-in only — never selected by default; when neither the flag nor the env var is set the binary keeps its existing domain behavior unchanged. A `--site-dir <PATH>` override is also parsed for use by SHB-003. NAT port-mapping (Tier 1) depends on the `upnp` cargo feature, which MUST remain non-default (`upnp = ["scp-transport/upnp"]` is already declared in `crates/scp-node/Cargo.toml` and absent from `[features].default`); this story only verifies that invariant and does not change defaults. This is the entry-point selection story; the Supervisor/relay wiring is SHB-002, payload publication is SHB-003.
acceptanceCriteria: main.rs parses a `--self-host` flag: `cargo run -p scp-node -- --help` prints a `--self-host` line (assert via test `self_host_flag_in_usage` grepping the usage string)

main.rs reads `SCP_NODE_SELF_HOST`: when set to `1` and no `--self-host` flag is passed, self-host mode is selected (test `self_host_env_selects_mode` asserts the parsed CliConfig self_host field is true)
Self-host mode is opt-in: when neither `--self-host` nor `SCP_NODE_SELF_HOST` is set, the parsed CliConfig self_host field is false (test `self_host_defaults_off`)

Self-host mode does NOT require `SCP_NODE_DOMAIN`: a test `self_host_does_not_require_domain` constructs CliConfig from args `["--self-host"]` with no domain env and asserts no error is returned for the missing-domain case
main.rs parses `--site-dir <PATH>` into the CliConfig site_dir field: test `site_dir_override_parsed` asserts the path is captured
`grep -c 'default' crates/scp-node/Cargo.toml` shows the `[features]` `default` list does NOT contain `upnp` (CI command: `grep -A2 '^default' crates/scp-node/Cargo.toml | grep -qv upnp`)
`grep -q 'upnp = \["scp-transport/upnp"\]' crates/scp-node/Cargo.toml` confirms the non-default `upnp` feature is declared
actionItems: Add `self_host: bool` and `site_dir: Option<PathBuf>` fields to CliConfig in main.rs
Parse `--self-host` flag and `SCP_NODE_SELF_HOST` env var (flag OR env selects the mode)
Parse `--site-dir <PATH>` argument into site_dir
Add `--self-host`, `--site-dir`, and `SCP_NODE_SELF_HOST` lines to the printed usage/help text
Make the domain requirement conditional: domain is only mandated on the non-self-host path
Add tests: self_host_flag_in_usage, self_host_env_selects_mode, self_host_defaults_off, self_host_does_not_require_domain, site_dir_override_parsed

stories.title: Run an in-process Supervisor on a loopback relay for the self-host publish path
stories.description: Self-host mode must publish broadcast site assets and then project them. The publish path requires a protocol participant (a Supervisor / ContextManager) connected to a relay so that `BroadcastContent` assets can be PUBLISHed before `commit_deploy` projects them. This story builds the self-host run path in main.rs: construct an `ApplicationNode` via `ApplicationNodeBuilder::no_domain()` (per §10.12.8) AND an in-process Supervisor connected to the node's own loopback relay, sharing the same blob storage backend so a publish on the Supervisor side is visible to `commit_deploy` on the node side. This closes the publish -> commit_deploy loop. Asset publication and projection activation are SHB-003; this story is the runtime wiring (no_domain node + loopback-relay-connected Supervisor) only.
acceptanceCriteria: Self-host run path constructs the node via `ApplicationNodeBuilder::no_domain()`: `grep -q 'no_domain()' crates/scp-node/src/main.rs` returns true on the self-host code path

Self-host run path constructs an in-process Supervisor connected to the node's loopback relay: test `self_host_supervisor_connects_loopback_relay` asserts the Supervisor's transport target resolves to a `127.0.0.1`/`::1` relay address

The Supervisor and the node share the same blob storage backend instance (test `self_host_shared_blob_backend` asserts an asset published via the Supervisor is readable by the node-side projection lookup against the same backend)

Self-host run path does NOT call `.domain()` or provision ACME TLS (test `self_host_skips_acme` asserts no TLS provisioning is invoked on the self-host path; verified via a mock/no-op TlsProvider receiving zero calls)
Integration test `self_host_publish_then_commit_closes_loop` publishes one BroadcastContent asset through the Supervisor and asserts `commit_deploy` on the node finds it (non-empty path index)
actionItems: Add a `run_self_host` function in main.rs guarded by the self_host CliConfig field
Build the ApplicationNode with `ApplicationNodeBuilder::no_domain()` and a shared `Arc` blob storage backend
Construct an in-process Supervisor/ContextManager connected to the node's loopback relay using the shared backend
Add tests: self_host_supervisor_connects_loopback_relay, self_host_shared_blob_backend, self_host_skips_acme, self_host_publish_then_commit_closes_loop

sources.section: ## ADR-035: Local HTTP Control API and Broadcast Projection

stories.title: Publish embedded/--site-dir static payload as BroadcastContent assets and project the site
stories.description: With the publish path open (SHB-002), self-host mode must take a static payload, publish each asset as a `BroadcastContent` message, enable site projection, and commit a deploy so the node serves the site over HTTP (§18.11.12 SiteConfig, ADR-042 broadcast content delivery). The default payload is embedded from `crates/scp-node/assets/selfhost/` (`index.html`, `style.css`, `app.js` already exist); `--site-dir <PATH>` (parsed in SHB-001) overrides the default to read assets from disk. The run path creates a broadcast context, publishes each asset via the Supervisor, calls `enable_broadcast_projection_with_site` with a `SiteConfig`, and calls `commit_deploy` to build the immutable `path -> blob_id` index. Per §18.11.12, `index_path` defaults to `/index.html`.
acceptanceCriteria: Default payload is embedded from `crates/scp-node/assets/selfhost/`: test `self_host_embeds_default_assets` asserts the embedded `index.html`, `style.css`, and `app.js` byte slices are non-empty

`--site-dir <PATH>` overrides the embedded payload: test `self_host_site_dir_overrides_embedded` writes a temp dir with a distinct `index.html` and asserts the published asset bytes match the on-disk file, not the embedded default
Each asset is published as a BroadcastContent message via the Supervisor: test `self_host_publishes_each_asset` asserts one published blob per source file
Site projection is enabled via `enable_broadcast_projection_with_site` with a non-None SiteConfig: `grep -q 'enable_broadcast_projection_with_site' crates/scp-node/src/main.rs` returns true
`commit_deploy` is called and produces a path index containing `/index.html`: test `self_host_commit_deploy_indexes_index_html` asserts `/index.html` is present in the committed index
SiteConfig index_path defaults to `/index.html` per §18.11.12 (test `self_host_site_config_index_path_default` asserts the SiteConfig index_path equals `/index.html`)
actionItems: Embed `assets/selfhost/{index.html,style.css,app.js}` via `include_bytes!`/`include_str!`
When site_dir is Some, read assets from disk instead of the embedded defaults
Create a broadcast context and publish each asset as a BroadcastContent message via the Supervisor
Call `enable_broadcast_projection_with_site` with a SiteConfig (index_path `/index.html`)
Call `commit_deploy` to build and swap in the path index
Add tests: self_host_embeds_default_assets, self_host_site_dir_overrides_embedded, self_host_publishes_each_asset, self_host_commit_deploy_indexes_index_html, self_host_site_config_index_path_default

stories.title: Loud opt-in startup disclosure of public-port exposure, IP-DID linkage, and plaintext transit
stories.description: Self-host mode opens the node's public HTTP port to the internet via NAT port-mapping and publishes the operator's residential IP into the DHT-stored DID document (§10.12.9 'Residential IP exposure in DID document'), all over plaintext `ws://`/`http://` (§10.12.9 'Network metadata exposure without TLS', §10.12.6). The operator must be made explicitly aware. On startup of self-host mode, the binary MUST emit a loud, legible disclosure stating: (1) a public TCP port is being opened to the internet; (2) the operator's IP becomes publicly bound to their DID (an IP<->DID dox); (3) transit is plaintext (no TLS on the no_domain path). The disclosure is gated to self-host mode only and never printed on the default domain path.
acceptanceCriteria: Self-host startup emits a disclosure naming public-port exposure: test `self_host_discloses_public_port` asserts the startup disclosure string contains the bound public port and the phrase indicating it is opened to the public internet
Disclosure names the IP<->DID linkage: test `self_host_discloses_ip_did_dox` asserts the disclosure string references the operator IP being published into the DID document
Disclosure names plaintext transit: test `self_host_discloses_plaintext` asserts the disclosure string references plaintext / no-TLS transit
Disclosure is gated to self-host mode: test `non_self_host_omits_disclosure` asserts the disclosure is NOT emitted on the default domain path
Disclosure is emitted before the NAT mapping is opened (test `disclosure_precedes_nat_mapping` asserts the disclosure is produced prior to the port-mapping call in the self-host run sequence)
actionItems: Add a `self_host_disclosure(public_port, did, bind_ip) -> String` helper in main.rs
Emit the disclosure via `tracing::warn!` (or eprintln) at the start of the self-host run path, before NAT mapping
Cover the three required facts: public port opened, IP<->DID linkage, plaintext transit
Add tests: self_host_discloses_public_port, self_host_discloses_ip_did_dox, self_host_discloses_plaintext, non_self_host_omits_disclosure, disclosure_precedes_nat_mapping

stories.title: Release the NAT mapping on shutdown and keep dev/bridge endpoints loopback-only
stories.description: Self-host mode opens an inbound NAT port mapping (§10.12.2). On clean shutdown the mapping MUST be released so the operator's router does not retain a stale public forward after the process exits; where the underlying mapping is a one-shot lease that cannot be explicitly deleted, that limitation MUST be logged at shutdown rather than silently ignored. Separately, the node's dev/control and bridge endpoints MUST NOT be exposed to the public internet by self-host mode: the dev API already restricts itself to loopback hosts (`dev_api::ALLOWED_HOSTS = ["localhost", "127.0.0.1", "[::1]"]`) — this story verifies that self-host mode does not bind the dev/bridge endpoints to the public address and that they remain loopback-only or authenticated. This is the teardown + endpoint-exposure hardening story.
acceptanceCriteria: On clean shutdown the self-host path calls the port-mapping release: test `self_host_releases_mapping_on_shutdown` asserts the unmap/release call is invoked on the shutdown sequence (verified via a mock PortMapper recording an unmap call)
If the mapping is a non-releasable one-shot lease, a shutdown log states the limitation: test `self_host_logs_lease_limitation` asserts the limitation message is emitted when release is unsupported

Self-host mode does NOT bind the dev API to the public address: test `self_host_dev_api_loopback_only` asserts the dev API bind address is a loopback address (`is_loopback()` true) under self-host mode
`grep -q 'ALLOWED_HOSTS' crates/scp-node/src/dev_api.rs` confirms the loopback-only host allowlist is enforced for the dev API

Self-host mode does NOT expose the bridge/control endpoint on the public address: test `self_host_bridge_endpoint_not_public` asserts the bridge endpoint (if started) binds loopback only or requires authentication
actionItems: Hold the PortMapping handle from the no_domain build and release it in the self-host shutdown sequence
When release is unsupported (one-shot lease), log the limitation at shutdown
Ensure the dev API bind address under self-host mode is loopback-only (do not bind to the public HTTP address)
Verify bridge/control endpoints are loopback-only or authenticated under self-host mode
Add tests: self_host_releases_mapping_on_shutdown, self_host_logs_lease_limitation, self_host_dev_api_loopback_only, self_host_bridge_endpoint_not_public

stories.title: Integration test: in-process publish -> commit -> HTTP GET serves the site
stories.description: End-to-end proof that self-host mode serves a real site without any external network. An integration test stands up the self-host run path entirely in-process (loopback relay + Supervisor + node, no NAT mapping required), publishes the embedded payload, enables projection, commits a deploy, then performs an HTTP GET against the node's loopback HTTP server at the site route and asserts the served plaintext bytes equal the published `index.html`. This is the acceptance gate for the whole feature: it exercises SHB-002 (publish path), SHB-003 (asset publication + projection), and confirms the served output (ADR-042 broadcast content delivery, §18.11.12 SiteConfig).
acceptanceCriteria: Test file `crates/scp-node/tests/self_host_e2e.rs` exists and is exercised by `cargo test -p scp-node --test self_host_e2e`
Test `self_host_e2e_serves_index` stands up the in-process self-host path (loopback relay + Supervisor + node), publishes the embedded payload, enables projection, and commits a deploy
Test performs an HTTP GET against the node's loopback site route for `/index.html` and asserts HTTP 200
Test asserts the served response body bytes equal the published `index.html` bytes (plaintext, server-side decrypted)
Test asserts the served `Content-Type` for `/index.html` is `text/html`
`DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$(python3.12 -c "import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_config_var('LIBDIR'))") cargo test -p scp-node --test self_host_e2e` passes
actionItems: Create `crates/scp-node/tests/self_host_e2e.rs`
Build the in-process self-host path (loopback relay, Supervisor, node sharing a blob backend)
Publish embedded assets, enable projection with SiteConfig, commit_deploy
GET the loopback site route for `/index.html`, assert 200 + body equals published bytes + Content-Type text/html
Add test self_host_e2e_serves_index
